title: Grove's own rate limit can allow an Ethena mint that still fails because Ethena's per-block limits are shared with other users
content:
A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.2.2.1.2.1.2.10.3.2 carries an unusual admission: "Note that Ethena's per-block mint limits are shared with other users, so a mint may still fail even when the `RateLimits` allow the `usdcAmount`." A...10.4.2 repeats it for redemption.

The distinction being drawn is between a **budget** and a **guarantee**. Grove's `RateLimits` are a self-imposed ceiling on its own activity; Ethena's per-block limits are a shared resource contended for by every other participant. Passing the first says nothing about the second.

The operational implication is that a relayer's failed mint is not necessarily evidence of misconfiguration on Grove's side, and — more importantly — that Grove's exit path is contended too. In a stress event where many holders want to redeem USDe at once, the same shared per-block limit that throttles everyone throttles Grove, exactly when Grove most wants to move.

Documenting the gap in the Artifact rather than in a code comment is the notable part: it makes the residual risk a governance-visible fact about the integration rather than a surprise discovered during an incident.
description: The Atlas records this explicitly for both mint and redeem: a local control cannot guarantee capacity at a counterparty whose throughput is a common resource.
